paper.title_en: Higgs production in association with a Z boson at TeV-scale lepton colliders
paper.abstract_en: We study kinematical properties of the process <math altimg="si14.svg"><mrow><msup><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><msup><mi>l</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>→</mo><mi>ν</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>Z</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></math> at future TeV-scale lepton colliders. We classify the Feynman amplitudes into three main topological categories: vector-boson scattering, <math altimg="si15.svg"><mrow><msup><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></math> scattering, and <math altimg="si16.svg"><mrow><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><msup><mi>l</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></math> scattering contributions, and analyze the interference patterns among these amplitudes in both the recently proposed Feynman-diagram (FD) gauge and the conventional unitary gauge. We demonstrate that the rapidity distributions of the Z boson closely resemble those in <math altimg="si17.svg"><mrow><msup><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><msup><mi>l</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>→</mo><mi>ν</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>Z</mi></mrow></math>, while the Higgs-boson rapidity distribution is significantly different: Higgs bosons are produced nearly isotropically, whereas longitudinally polarized Z bosons are enhanced in the forward and backward regions. We find that this difference is traced to the topology-dependent structure of the FD-gauge amplitudes. We also demonstrate that suitable kinematical cuts can isolate specific subamplitudes, enabling partial FD-gauge amplitudes to effectively describe physical distributions.
